title: Steering Vector Staleness x Continuous Deployment: A Drift-Monitoring Harness Prototype

original_idea.body: Build a harness that, given two checkpoints and a stored steering vector, computes concept-direction drift and effect drop and emits a recalibrate flag.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible safety-infra chain (drift detector prevents silent failure) but depends on steering being deployed; modest link.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Building a drift-monitoring harness + LoRA checkpoints is guided engineering; novice + mentor feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable (harness) but requires creating fine-tuned checkpoints and validating the flag.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Reusable drift-detection infra for the open community, addresses explicit open problem; no internal access.

low_compute.reasoning: Small LoRA fine-tunes + inference; single GPU days.

novelty.reasoning: A drift-detection harness for steering vectors across checkpoints appears largely unexplored.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: A concrete steering-vector drift-monitoring harness with recalibrate trigger is an underexplored buildable contribution.
